summary: Make limiting arguments precise enough to recognize when an approximation or interchange of limits is justified.
outcomes: Use quantified definitions of sequence convergence and continuity
Distinguish pointwise from uniform convergence with counterexamples
sequence: Place a sequence inside shrinking error bounds
Write and interpret an epsilon definition
Compare convergence with boundedness and completeness
Contrast pointwise and uniform convergence of functions
Test a tempting interchange of limit and integral

visual.question: Can every point eventually settle while no single bound works everywhere?
visual.interaction: Increase the sequence index and inspect both pointwise error and worst-case error

practice.task: Prove a simple convergence claim and diagnose an invalid limit interchange
practice.success: Quantifiers are ordered correctly and any theorem used has its hypotheses checked
